etymologies.heading: Etymology 1
paragraphs: From Latin pontificatus, from pontifex (“high priest”), from pons (“bridge”) + facere (“make”).
senses: The status or term of office of a pontiff or pontifex.

etymologies.heading: Etymology 2
paragraphs: From the past participle stem of Medieval Latin pontificō, from Latin pontifex (“high priest”), from pons (“bridge”) + facere (“make”).
senses: (intransitive) To preside as a bishop, especially at mass.
(intransitive) To act like a pontiff; to express one's position or opinions dogmatically and pompously as if they were absolutely correct.
